newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat price surge seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat price surge seen continuing.

text.p: Turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange was low on Monday mainly because milling wheat futures prices will be freed on Tuesday after limit rises today and last week, dealers said.
"Nobody wanted to sell at current levels as everybody expects prices to jump on Tuesday," said Sandor Torok of Agrokont.
Two milling wheat positions freed on Friday surged 710 forints per tonne to 27,080 for January and 700 for March to end at 27,500.
All other positions rose the daily 400 forints limit with August closing at 22,470 forints, October at 23,750 and May at 26,680.
"To achieve a normal spread, August milling wheat has to rise to around 25,000 forints," Torok said.
Milling wheat prices rose over the last week due to fears that heavy rains, which also delayed harvesting, would lower the crop's quality.
Current weather forecasts point to scattered showers over the northern half of Hungary and moderate to heavy rains throughout the country by Friday.
Torok said milling wheat prices will only stabilise when figures about crop quality are available.
Milling wheat also rose on increased export hopes, as flood-stricken Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia were likely to need imports, traders said.
A west European analyst said earlier today Poland might need up to 1.5 million tonnes of mainly high-quality grain.
Feed wheat prices went limit-down on Monday for the same reason of expectations of a low quality Hungarian crop, Torok said.
"There will be unsellable amounts of feed wheat (after harvesting)," he said.
Feed wheat went limit-down for all positions to end between 17,500 forints for August and 18,500 for December. March opened at 19,000 forints.
Elsewhere on the market, maize prices dropped between 100 and 330 forints except steady March and May.
Feed barley remained steady and tradeless except August which eased 40 forints to 17,350 and October which edged up 10 forints to 18,610.
Total grains turnover edged up but was still at a below-average 694 lots, or 289 million forints compared to Friday's 481 lots or 221.4 million forints.
